features: ALWAYS A4, NEVER A3 — An administrator compared, on paper, KondoManager's apportionment by table with the one from his previous software: with more than five tables ours came out in A3, which no home printer has, and reprinted on A4 it was unreadable and on two pages. The two apportionment prints, by table and by chapter, now always come out in landscape A4: tight margins, 7-point body up to six columns, compact cells. A building with 38 units and 48 rows fits in two pages, where before it took two A3 pages and four.

BALANCED BLOCKS, TOTALS ONCE — With many tables the print splits the columns into balanced page blocks (ten tables make 5 + 5, not 8 + 2); the block carrying the totals never exceeds six tables, because with seven or eight the numbers did not fit. The grand-total columns and row appear only in the last block; earlier blocks close with their own column totals and say so at the bottom. Before, every block repeated the document totals and the second page stated a total its columns contradicted.

READ IN THE ORDER OF THE BUILDING — Rows come out by unit number in natural order ("2" before "10", "4 bis" between "4" and "5"), then units without a number by name. The unit cell has the name on top and a single small line underneath ("int. 3 · piano 1"), only when there is something to write: a garage without a number no longer prints an empty "Int. —", and a floor entered as a bare number gets its label.

THE FILE HAS A NAME, THE RESPONSE HAS A BODY — Instalment schedule, apportionment by table and by chapter download as "riparto-tabelle-<building>-2026.pdf" and the like, instead of "prospetto_rate.pdf" for all. Underneath was a silent defect: mPDF wrote the PDF straight to the output and the response stayed empty; the browser saw the file, a test did not. Now the response carries the bytes.

SIGNATURE AND FOOTER WITHIN THE MARGIN — In the two apportionment prints the administrator's signature sits on one line with its label, lower: before, it ended up alone on a blank third page. The page footer has a compact variant that fits in the 7 mm of the margin: the standard one measures 10.6 and its rule cut through the last row and the signature.

DETAILS YOU SEE ON PAPER — In the apportionment by chapter the shares follow the table's decimals, as in the apportionment by table (before they were a fixed three and "159,570" broke across lines). "TOT. SOGG." and "mill. ‰" stay on one line; role percentages use the comma; the legend also declares the bare owner and the real units of measure of the columns; bare ownership sits next to the owner in both prints.

A TEST BUILDING WITH THE SHAPE OF A REAL ONE — 38 units, 48 rows, six tables, five budget chapters for € 18,350.00, rented flats and garages, couples under a single name, a company among the tenants: the shape is the one reported, the data is made up. Eighteen tests use it, reading format and page count from the PDF itself rather than from template variables.

WHAT REMAINS — In the apportionment by chapter an "Unallocated" column of € 0.01 shows on some rows: the cents the role cascade does not assign when an item is split 66.67/33.33. It is Code 77/78, which beta.28 closes with the persisted apportionment detail.
